checkpoints.section: Power threats and why they differ
checkpoints.question: What is the key difference between a voltage sag and a brownout?

options.A: A voltage sag causes processor errors and data loss, while a brownout causes equipment to shut down immediately
options.B: A brownout is typically caused by lightning strikes, while a voltage sag is caused by grid overload conditions
options.C: A voltage sag is a sustained reduction in voltage over time, while a brownout is a brief dip in voltage lasting milliseconds to seconds
options.D: A brownout is a sustained reduction in voltage over time, while a voltage sag is a brief dip in voltage lasting milliseconds to seconds

checkpoints.explanation: The section explicitly defines a brownout as a sustained voltage reduction and a voltage sag as a brief dip (milliseconds to seconds), making duration the distinguishing factor.

checkpoints.section: UPS architecture: three tiers of protection
checkpoints.question: Which UPS architecture provides zero transfer time during an outage?

options.A: Line-Interactive UPS uses an autotransformer that provides instantaneous switching
options.B: Offline/Standby UPS uses a transfer switch that engages in zero milliseconds
options.C: Online/Double-Conversion UPS always runs equipment from the inverter continuously
options.D: All three architectures achieve zero transfer time through different mechanisms

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that Online/Double-Conversion UPS has zero transfer time because equipment always runs from the inverter; there is no gap when the grid fails.

checkpoints.question: What is the typical service life of a VRLA battery before capacity degrades and replacement is needed?

options.A: VRLA batteries typically last three to five years before replacement is required
options.B: VRLA batteries typically last six to twelve months before replacement is required
options.C: VRLA batteries typically last eight to ten years before replacement is required
options.D: VRLA batteries typically last one to two years before replacement is required

checkpoints.explanation: The section explicitly states that VRLA batteries have a service life of 3–5 years, then capacity degrades and replacement is required.

checkpoints.question: What does an NMC (Network Management Card) in a UPS enable?

options.A: An NMC manages fuel levels in connected diesel generators remotely
options.B: An NMC exposes UPS status information over the network via SNMP protocol
options.C: An NMC isolates individual outlets from power distribution during overload events
options.D: An NMC automatically restarts failed servers when battery power runs low

checkpoints.explanation: The section defines the NMC as a card that exposes status (load, battery charge, alarms) over the network via SNMP.

checkpoints.section: Generators: extending runtime from minutes to days
checkpoints.question: What is the primary difference between diesel and natural gas generators in terms of fuel availability?

options.A: Diesel generators connect to a utility network for continuous fuel supply, while natural gas requires bulk storage tanks on-site
options.B: Diesel generators can be refueled faster than natural gas generators during an emergency situation
options.C: Natural gas generators connect to a utility gas network for continuous fuel supply, while diesel requires bulk storage tanks on-site
options.D: Both types require the same maintenance schedule and fuel management procedures every six months

checkpoints.explanation: The section states that natural gas generators connect to the utility gas network (effectively unlimited fuel) while diesel requires on-site bulk storage that degrades in 6–12 months.

checkpoints.section: Redundant power distribution and data center tiers
checkpoints.question: In a dual power feed configuration, what does each power supply connect to to eliminate single points of failure?

options.A: Each supply connects to both a generator and a UPS to provide redundancy across multiple power sources
options.B: Each supply connects to a separate PDU, separate circuit, and ideally separate utility feeds from different substations
options.C: Each supply connects to a shared power panel and the same utility transformer substation for load balancing
options.D: Each supply connects to the same PDU and circuit breaker to minimize equipment and installation complexity

checkpoints.explanation: The section explicitly states that dual power feeds connect each supply to a separate PDU, separate circuit, separate panel, and ideally a separate utility feed from a different substation.

checkpoints.section: Redundant power distribution and data center tiers
checkpoints.question: What availability percentage does Uptime Institute Tier III data center power redundancy provide?

options.A: Tier III provides approximately 99.982% availability per year
options.B: Tier III provides approximately 99.995% availability per year
options.C: Tier III provides approximately 98.5% availability per year
options.D: Tier III provides approximately 99.671% availability per year

checkpoints.explanation: The section's Uptime Institute Tier classification table explicitly states that Tier III provides 99.982% availability.
